subject: Veridian runtime degradation — exec liaison & customer bridge
messages:
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Veridian runtime anomaly — initial bridge request

Team —

We have an active degradation impacting a subset of Veridian traffic hitting our inference pool in us-west-2. Symptoms: elevated tail latency (p95->>3.2s), increased error rate on streaming endpoints, and intermittent OOMs on a small fraction of GPU workers. Impact is customer-facing for Veridian (prod) — roughly ~7% of requests route through impacted nodes.

Actions taken so far:
- Auto-scaling triggered additional instances but some failed to boot and fell back to older kernels.
- We opened a bridge with infra and started log aggregation (attached: bridge_log_snippets.txt).
- Hotfix candidate: disable a new kernel optimization rolled last week (possible regression).

Need:
- Kimberly, can you lead customer liaison and send an initial customer-facing update?
- Markus, please draft an exec note (quick bullet) we can send to Maya if this escalates.
- Laura, heads-up for potential credits / SLA discussion.

I'll continue with the ops bridge and push a rollback test.

Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Incident Responder — Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: ops@veridian.ai
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Veridian runtime degradation — immediate update and impact summary

Maya / Veridian Ops —

This is Kimberly from Redwood Inference. I’m writing to confirm we are actively managing a degradation affecting a portion of your production traffic in us-west-2. Short summary:

- What happened: an internal runtime regression introduced last week is triggering elevated GPU memory pressure and causing intermittent OOMs on ~7% of Veridian requests routed to us-west-2 pool.
- User impact: increased latency (p95 from ~1s to ~3s) and occasional request failures for the affected shard. We are not seeing data leakage; this is a runtime stability issue.
- Mitigation in progress: we are testing a rollback of the kernel optimization that was onboarded last week and diverting new Veridian requests away from affected workers.
- ETA & next update cadence: aiming for a mitigant test complete within 60 minutes; I will provide a status update at 10:20 PT and another at 12:00 PT or earlier if we restore service.

Immediate asks for Veridian ops:
- Please confirm any high-priority customer flows we should prioritize when we apply routing rules.
- If you have recent traffic patterns or any changes on your side in the last 48 hours that could correlate, share those logs.

We will follow up with an executive-facing brief for Maya once we validate mitigation. Attaching initial logs for transparency (bridge_log_snippets.txt).

Contacts:
Ben Carter — Incident lead (ben_carter@redwood.com)
Kimberly Park — Customer liaison / Exec comms (kimberly_park@redwood.com)
Markus Klein — Engineering lead (markus_klein@redwood.com)

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
phone: +1 (415) 555-0124

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Exec note draft for Maya (Veridian)

Kimberly / Laura —

Draft executive note below (concise, for Maya). Use as-is or edit for tone. I’ll be available on the bridge for technical Q&A.

--- DRAFT ---
Maya —

We are actively addressing a runtime regression that is impacting a subset of Veridian production traffic in our us-west-2 pool. Our immediate priority is restoring stable processing for all Veridian requests.

What we know: the issue appears linked to a kernel optimization change deployed last week that increases memory residency under certain sequence-length distributions. This has produced intermittent OOMs and elevated tail latency for ~7% of traffic.

Immediate steps: rollback candidate is being tested now; we are diverting traffic away from affected workers and increasing cache affinity to reduce memory pressure. We expect the first mitigant result within 60 minutes.

Commitments:
- We will provide a technical postmortem within 72 hours with root cause, corrective actions, and timeline for any compensatory measures (if warranted).
- We will supply a replay of logs and traces for your SRE team on request.

Contact: Kimberly Park (Director, Customer Reliability) — kimberly_park@redwood.com.

We recommend offering Maya a short 15-minute call after mitigation to answer questions and confirm next steps.

--- end draft ---

LMK and I’ll send once Kimberly signs off.

Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Runtime Engineering — Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: maya.singh@veridian.ai
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Veridian — executive status update and commitment (10:22 PT)

Maya —

Following up with an executive status update. We’ve initiated the rollback of a kernel optimization that appears to be the likely root cause of elevated memory pressure and OOMs affecting a subset of your traffic in us-west-2.

Status (10:22 PT):
- Mitigant test underway: rollback candidate applied to a canary subset (5% of affected workers). Early telemetry shows decreased OOMs in the canary cluster; p95 latency trending down.
- Traffic routing: we have applied temporary routing rules to shift new sessions away from impacted workers.
- Customer impact: reduced but not fully resolved — we remain in degraded state for a small shard; overall user impact is limited to ~7% of requests.
- Safety & data: there is no evidence of data loss or exposure.

What to expect next:
- We will monitor canary for 30–45 minutes. If stable, we will roll the mitigant cluster-wide and expect full recovery within 60–90 minutes from now.
- After stability, we will schedule a 15-minute call to walk through timelines, provide logs/traces, and discuss compensatory options if required.

Attachments: veridian_exec_brief.pdf (high-level timeline and next steps)

I’ll send another update at 12:00 PT or earlier on any change. Please reply here if you’d prefer a quick call sooner; we can be on a bridge in under 10 minutes.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124
